## C2 - Confusables and KG hints, Belts

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Belts bind driver plus every rider with under-eighteens double-locked, while only a physician's signed waiver for real medical cause can unbind [A01].
Why it matters: group belt-scope; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F02, sec12-F04 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Lap straps ride low on thighs and shoulders cross the chest snug, never behind backs or under arms, with pregnancy belting lowest of all [A01].
Why it matters: group belt-fit; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec12-F03 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Stops open with parking, flashers, dome lights, and killed gadgets, then freeze with belts on and hands wheeled [A01].
Why it matters: group stop-sequence; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F05, sec12-F06 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: FXsec12R04
Tell the officer where your license, registration and insurance are, then retrieve them slowly while one hand stays on the wheel. You may request identification from an ununiformed officer or one in an unmarked vehicle. Signing a citation does not admit guilt; refusing may lead to arrest or a required visit to the station [FXsec12R04].
Why it matters: group stop-paperwork; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F07, sec12-F08 [FXsec12R04].
Source: [FXsec12R04 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
Officers may land driver-side or passenger-side, and roadside arguments lose everywhere since court owns disputes [A01].
Why it matters: group stop-sides; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec12-F05, sec12-F08 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: FXsec12R06
A physician may excuse child-restraint use for weight, physical fitness or other medical reasons with a signed statement identifying the child and grounds carried by the transporter. A first offense brings a fifty-dollar fine; another offense may bring a five-hundred-dollar penalty [FXsec12R06].
Why it matters: group child-waiver-fine; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F09 [FXsec12R06].
Source: [FXsec12R06 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
Laps crush children against dashes, luggage bays and open hatches endanger riders, and pickup beds ban under-sixteens outright [A02].
Why it matters: group child-bans; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F10, sec12-F11 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
Doors run shut, locked, and child-locked with full halts for openings, while seats install safest center-back with check events verifying [A02].
Why it matters: group child-doors; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec12-F10 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
Bags only pillow belted riders, and demand ten-inch wheel gaps, downward tilts, and twelve-and-unders behind [A02].
Why it matters: group airbag-seating; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F12, sec12-F13 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A02
Birth to two rides rear-facing to maker bounds, then forward seats and boosters hold until eight or all seven fit tests pass [A02].
Why it matters: group seat-direction; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F14, sec12-F15 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: FXsec12R11
If there is no back seat, a rear-facing child seat may go in front only when the passenger airbag is absent or disabled. Children twelve and younger are safer restrained in the back seat [FXsec12R11].
Why it matters: group seat-position; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F14, sec12-F13 [FXsec12R11].
Source: [FXsec12R11 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]
